name: Aldford
worldBackground: Aldford is a quiet farming hamlet of a dozen households huddled at the tree line of the Eldenwood, its days measured by the turning of the millwheel on the stream. The chapel bell, the smell of barley and the low murmur of the inn's common room mark the rhythm of life here. Trouble brews quietly: the miller has begun charging a heavier toll per sack than custom allows, and the farmers whisper about withholding their grain come harvest.

setting.technology: pre-industrial: water power, hand tools, animal transport
setting.climate: temperate, mild wet summers and cold damp winters

templates.name: Straw bed
templates.description: A wooden frame strung with rope and stuffed with a straw palliasse, the standard bed of every Aldford household.
templates.physicalDescription: A narrow rectangle of dark timber with a pale straw mattress and a folded woollen blanket at the foot.
templates.rule: One per sleeper: place in a corner of every cottage and farmhouse away from the hearth; inn guest rooms get one against a wall with a chest at its foot.

templates.name: Wooden table
templates.description: A scarred plank table on trestle legs, used for meals, mending and the miller's tally-keeping alike.
templates.physicalDescription: A long pale-brown rectangle of planks seen from above.
templates.rule: One table in each cottage great room near the hearth; the inn common room gets several spaced apart so stools can ring them.

templates.name: Three-legged stool
templates.description: A humble cut-log stool that serves at table, hearth and milking stool alike.
templates.physicalDescription: A small round seat with three splayed legs.
templates.rule: Cluster stools around tables and beside the inn hearth, never blocking a doorway or the path to the stairs.

templates.name: Plank bench
templates.description: A long backless bench that seats the chapel congregation, the inn's common room and idlers on the green.
templates.physicalDescription: A narrow brown rectangle of planks.
templates.rule: Set benches in rows facing the chapel altar, along the sides of inn common room tables, and one on the green directly in front of the inn door.

templates.name: Stone altar
templates.description: The rough-hewn altar of St. Brannoc, draped in linen for Sunday services and harvest blessings.
templates.physicalDescription: A pale grey rectangular slab with a small white cloth square at its centre.
templates.rule: One only, against the chapel's east wall, with clear floor between it and the bench rows.

templates.name: Stone hearth
templates.description: An open fireplace of fieldstone that cooks the barley pottage and warms every dwelling in the hamlet.
templates.physicalDescription: A blackened grey block with a dark fire opening and ash scatter in front.
templates.rule: One per dwelling built against a wall, kept well clear of beds and stored grain, with the table nearby.

templates.name: Storage chest
templates.description: An iron-bound oak chest holding clothing, grain, herbs or the inn's spare candles.
templates.physicalDescription: A squat dark-brown box with a pale metal band across the lid.
templates.rule: One or two per home against a wall away from the hearth; one at the foot of every inn guest bed and two in the mill for flour records and tack.

templates.name: Forge and anvil
templates.description: The coal-fired smithy hearth with its anvil block, where horses are shod and scythes mended.
templates.physicalDescription: A blackened stone hearth square with a small dark anvil shape at one side.
templates.rule: One block against the smithy's back wall, with the quench trough and coal pile just outside the smithy door.

templates.name: Wooden trough
templates.description: A hollowed-trunk trough serving horses and cattle at the green and hot iron at the smithy.
templates.physicalDescription: A long open rectangle showing dark water or blackened interior.
templates.rule: The water trough stands beside the village well on the green; a second, blackened one sits at the smithy door as the quench trough; never place one indoors.

templates.name: Coal pile
templates.description: A heap of char brought up the mill track, hoarded for the smithy's fire.
templates.physicalDescription: A low dark-black mound.
templates.rule: One heap under a timber lean-to against the smithy's side wall, within a step of the forge.

templates.name: Millstone rig
templates.description: The great runner stone and wooden gearing that turn the stream's power into flour.
templates.physicalDescription: A fat pale-grey circle with dark timber gearing radiating to one side.
templates.rule: One only, centred in the mill on its stream side so the gears run to the waterwheel shaft, with grain sacks stacked in reach.

templates.name: Grain sack
templates.description: A bulging sack of barley waiting on the miller's toll, the small grievance that stirs the hamlet.
templates.physicalDescription: A lumpy beige square with a tied neck.
templates.rule: Stack in clusters of two to five inside the mill and on its loading dock, with a few in the threshing barn after harvest.

templates.name: Hay pile
templates.description: A golden haystack raised in the fields, or sheaves pitched under cover in the threshing barn.
templates.physicalDescription: A rounded golden-yellow mound with a darker thatched top.
templates.rule: Space haystacks across the barley flats behind the fences; line one interior wall of the threshing barn with hay piles clear of the central threshing floor.

templates.name: Scarecrow
templates.description: A straw man in a patched coat, standing his lonely watch over the barley.
templates.physicalDescription: A thin brown cross-pole with a pale ragged blob at its head.
templates.rule: One only, out mid-way in a barley strip away from the track, facing the field path.

templates.name: Split-rail fence
templates.description: Chestnut rails split by the woodsman and mortised into posts, penning the fields from the cattle.
templates.physicalDescription: A thin brown line of parallel rails with post nubs at each end.
templates.rule: Run linked segments along the field track and around the barley strips, leaving gaps where gates and the mill cart turning space fall.

templates.name: Farm cart
templates.description: A creaking wain for hay and sacks, drawn by oxen or left standing between tasks.
templates.physicalDescription: A brown rectangular bed with a long dark shaft extending from one side.
templates.rule: Park off the path: the hay cart beside the inn on the green, the ox cart at the edge of Odo's farmstead, never blocking a door or the track.

templates.name: Village well
templates.description: The stone-walled well on the green where all twelve households draw their water under gossiping breath.
templates.physicalDescription: A small grey ring of stone with a dark centre and two posts holding a tiny crossbar roof.
templates.rule: One public well only, on the village green within a few steps of inn and chapel; no other wells anywhere in Aldford.

templates.name: Stacked firewood
templates.description: Sawn and split logs stacked to dry, the woodsman's steady tribute to winter.
templates.physicalDescription: A tight rectangular block of pale cut-log ends.
templates.rule: Every cottage keeps a stack against a side wall under its eaves; taller stacks fill the clearing by the woodcutter's hut.

templates.name: Chopping stump
templates.description: A broad oak butt scarred by the axe, where logs are split for the hearth.
templates.physicalDescription: A pale round cut face ringed by flying wood chips.
templates.rule: Set beside a woodpile: one by the inn's stack on the green, one in the splitting area near the woodcutter's hut, never indoors.

templates.name: Broadleaf tree
templates.description: Great gnarled oaks of the Eldenwood and lone shade trees standing about the hamlet's edges.
templates.physicalDescription: A wide irregular green canopy with a darker trunk mark at its centre.
templates.rule: Cluster the huge old oaks through the Eldenwood clear of paths, scatter single trees along the forest edge and about the green, and set one leaning willow-like tree overhanging the millpond bank.

templates.name: Bush clump
templates.description: Thorn and hazel growth, trimmed into hedgerows between fields or left wild under the forest edge.
templates.physicalDescription: A small mottled dark-green clump.
templates.rule: String clumps into the low hedgerows dividing the barley strips and scatter them as undergrowth along the Eldenwood edge; never on the dirt track.

templates.name: Mossy boulder
templates.description: Old stones shrugged off by the forest, green-grown and patient.
templates.physicalDescription: A grey rounded lump with a paler moss cap on one side.
templates.rule: Only under forest canopy, half-sunk beside deer trails and fallen logs; never in ploughed ground or the village.

templates.name: Mushroom patch
templates.description: Pale caps sprouting in the damp leaf litter, gathered by Widow Maren against the winter.
templates.physicalDescription: A scatter of tiny cream dots over dark leaf mould.
templates.rule: Cluster patches on the dim forest floor near old oaks and fallen logs, never in open fields or the village green.

templates.name: Fallen log
templates.description: A wind-thrown trunk going soft with moss, home to beetles and shy deer at dusk.
templates.physicalDescription: A long grey-brown cylinder with a green moss stripe along one flank.
templates.rule: Scatter a few across the Eldenwood floor, some crossing the deer trails; never inside the village or on the farmland.

templates.name: Barley strip
templates.description: A strip of Aldford's gold crop, the backbone of every household's year and the miller's toll.
templates.physicalDescription: A dense golden-yellow field square with fine vertical combing.
templates.rule: Lay long strips side by side across the Barley Flats, separated by hedgerow, with the field track running along their edge and the farmsteads facing their crops.

templates.name: Dirt track
templates.description: Worn earth pressed bare by boots and cartwheels, the quiet veins of the hamlet.
templates.physicalDescription: A pale tan patch with faint parallel wheel-rut lines.
templates.rule: One main rutted strip runs from the green past the flats to the mill as the field track, with fainter threads winding through the trees as deer trails; never under buildings or water.

templates.name: Millpond and waterwheel
templates.description: The dark millpond feeding the great oak waterwheel whose steady turning measures Aldford's days.
templates.physicalDescription: A dark green-black water square with a huge brown spoked wheel circle on its mill-facing side.
templates.rule: One only, set against the mill's stream-side wall so the wheel face touches the mill; the loading dock runs along the pond beside it.

templates.name: Loading dock
templates.description: A plank platform over the pond's edge where sacks pass between cart, mill and boat.
templates.physicalDescription: A brown rectangular deck of parallel planks with dark water gaps showing between.
templates.rule: One only, hard against the mill's pond-facing wall beside the millpond, clear of the waterwheel's turn.

templates.name: Moored rowboat
templates.description: The miller's flat-bottomed skiff, tied and bobbing, for setting eel lines at dusk.
templates.physicalDescription: A narrow dark-hulled oval with a bench bar across its middle.
templates.rule: One only, tied at the millpond edge beside the loading dock, never mid-pond or out in the stream current.

templates.name: Staircase
templates.description: A tight winding stair of creaking treads climbing to the inn's guest lofts.
templates.physicalDescription: A small brown square of stacked step edges.
templates.rule: One only, inside the Sleeping Hart Inn against a wall near the common room hearth, linking the ground floor to the guest rooms above.

npcs.name: Aldous Fenwick
npcs.description: Aldous keeps four guest beds, two casks of autumn ale and every rumour in Aldford, and he wants the grain-toll quarrel kept off his benches because he fears a harvest boycott will empty his common room by Candlemas.
npcs.physicalDescription: Barrel-chested and balding, in a leather apron scorched at the hem, with a habit of wiping the same empty tankard for minutes at a stretch while he listens.

npcs.name: Osric Kemp
npcs.description: Osric has taken to demanding a ninth part of every sack instead of the customary tenth, wanting the coin to buy out his late brother's debt, and he worries the farmers will route their grain to some distant quern before first frost.
npcs.physicalDescription: Thick-set with flour-white forearms and a permanent dusting of meal in his black brows, and his right thumbnail is cracked from dragging sacks across the millstones' feeding trough.

npcs.name: Dunstan Wren
npcs.description: Dunstan walks from the field-edge cottage he shares with his young wife to the forge each dawn, wanting an apprentice before his eyes fail, and he worries the charcoal stack will not last a damp winter with every farmer suddenly demanding scythes and repointed ploughshares.
npcs.physicalDescription: Lean but knotted through the shoulders, arms cross-hatched with fresh burn scars, wearing a smoke-black leather shirt with one brass button gone green.

npcs.name: Father Ansel
npcs.role: priest of the Chapel of St. Brannoc
npcs.description: Ansel rents the small back room above the common room on parish ha'pennies and serves three cracked bells' worth of duty at the chapel, wanting to arbitrate between miller and farmers before the dispute ripens into sin, and he worries that whatever walks the Eldenwood after dusk is growing bolder each week.
npcs.physicalDescription: A thin grey man in a patched wool habit tied with rope, with ink stains on two fingers and a missing tooth he hides behind closed lips.

npcs.name: Maren Cobb
npcs.description: Maren tends every fever and foaling in Aldford from a shelf of thirty-two stoppered jars, wanting to lay in a winter store of elderberries and chamomile, and she worries that since midsummer something in the forest has been frightening the game away from her mushroom hollows.
npcs.physicalDescription: Small and bent at the shoulder, in layered grey shawls pinned with a fishbone brooch, and her left hand smells of comfrey no matter how she scrubs it.

npcs.name: Odo Blackbuck
npcs.description: Odo works nine strip-fields and a pair of heavy oxen, wanting the miller's toll cut back to the old tenth without ever saying so aloud, and he worries that if he is caught organizing the withholding he will be the first barred from the millstones come grinding season.
npcs.physicalDescription: Broad and slow-moving, in a sheepskin vest over a homespun tunic, with a horseshoe of white hair and a copper ring worn to a groove on his thumb.

npcs.name: Tibb Harrow
npcs.description: Tibb farms her late husband's two rented strips with three goats and two young sons underfoot, wanting her sheaves dry and her rent grain counted before the rains, and she worries the damp has already crept into the rick's heart and will rot half her winter bread.
npcs.physicalDescription: Weather-brown and wiry, hair bound in a red kerchief gone pale with washing, with a permanent grass stain along her right forearm from shouldering the scythe.

npcs.name: Hodge Fen
npcs.description: Hodge has stacked twenty-seven cords against his hut's north wall and wants forty before hard frost, but he worries about the deep quiet that has fallen on his usual cutting stand and the stripped bark he found at chest height on an oak last week.
npcs.physicalDescription: Tall and stooped from ducking boughs, in a smocked coat snagged at every seam, with a notched felling axe he carries even to the inn and a gold-less earring hole in one ear.

player.name: Ivo Marsh
player.description: Ivo's cart cracked its axle at the mill ford a week past, and he means to winter in the inn's common room mending pots, kettles and locks for coppers, wanting the smith to finish a seasoned oak axle before the roads turn to mud, and worrying that his pouch of eleven silver pennies will not outlast the snow.
player.physicalDescription: Slight and quick-fingered, in a travel-stained brown coat with a soldering iron and a coil of tin wire hanging at his belt, and a healing scorch across his left palm.
